title: The Timeout-After-Success Problem
hook: The request timed out after succeeding. Did it happen?
thesis: Distributed systems do not always know whether an external mutation occurred. Timeout-after-success is dangerous because blindly retrying a non-idempotent external mutation is incorrect. The episode publishes the lifecycle PING uses instead of the SUCCESS/FAILURE binary: PROPOSED, AUTHORIZED, CLAIMED, DISPATCHED, UNKNOWN, VERIFIED, RECONCILED, FAILED. Then it shows the reconciliation read: the concrete observation that resolves UNKNOWN into VERIFIED or RECONCILED without repeating the mutation.

proven: The directive states the full state vocabulary and the timeout-after-success danger (section 7).
The directive requires uncertain effects to reconcile instead of being blindly repeated (section 6).
partial: That the reconciliation read is implemented for the social engagement adapters named in the brief.
unknown: Measured examples of a timeout-after-success and its reconciliation in production logs.
